extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated industry, consumer groups, and other stakeholders who want to submit comments or petitions to FDA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to submit effective public comments on FDA proposed rules and how to prepare and submit citizen petitions (including required petition components and procedural rules). Covers submission methods, timing, content expectations, and privacy/public-record considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State your position and explain why
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly indicate if you are for or against the proposed rule or some part of it and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA reviewers look for reasoning, logic, and good science; be explicit about what you support or oppose and provide the rationale for your position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support comments with reasoning, logic, and scientific evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA regulatory decisions are based largely on law and science, and agency reviewers look for reasoning, logic, and good science in comments they evaluate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include arguments grounded in law, data, or peer-reviewed science where relevant; unsupported assertions are less persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference the docket number
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to the docket number, listed in Federal Register notice (i.e., FDA-20XX-X-XXXX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include the docket number for the proposed rule so your comment is associated with the correct regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting references and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a copy of articles or other references that support your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach supporting documents; note that electronic attachments will not be forwarded if the 'Comment' box is left empty — ensure the comment text box contains content if you want attachments forwarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit only relevant material
rubrics_metrics.description: Only relevant material should be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extraneous material; focused, relevant evidence and arguments are more useful to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide English translations for foreign-language materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If an article or reference is in a foreign language, it must be accompanied by an English translation verified to be accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations should be accompanied by a copy of the original publication; ensure translations are accurate and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect personal and patient privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: To protect privacy when submitting medical information, delete names or other information that would identify patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redact or anonymize personally identifiable information before submission; submissions become public records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware submissions become public records
rubrics_metrics.description: When a comment is received, it is logged in, numbered, and placed in a file for that docket; it then becomes a public record and is available for anyone to examine at regulations.gov or in FDA's public reading room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under FOIA, visitors can obtain copies (free up to 50 pages for noncommercial use; thereafter 10 cents per page). Consider confidentiality and privacy before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe the comment period and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register notice provides the 'comment period,' which specifies how long the agency will accept public comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment periods usually are open for 60 days but may be as short as 10 days or as long as nine months; weekends and holidays are included. Submit within the published period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use approved submission channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submission of comments is handled via Regulations.gov; petitions can be submitted electronically via Regulations.gov or mailed/delivered to Dockets Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA currently does not accept emailed petitions. Follow the Federal Dockets Management System Instruction Sheet for using Regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen petition required components (21 CFR 10.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizen Petitions under 21 CFR 10.30 must include: Action Request; Statement of Grounds; Environmental Impact; Economic Impact; Certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult 21 CFR 10.30 and sample formats in Title 21 for detailed instructions and required content; prepare petitions carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative reconsideration required components (21 CFR 10.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration petitions under 21 CFR 10.33 should state: Decision Involved; Action Required; Statement of Grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the procedural and content requirements in 21 CFR 10.33 when requesting administrative reconsideration of an action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative stay of action required components (21 CFR 10.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for an administrative stay under 21 CFR 10.35 should include: Decision Involved; Action Required; Statement of Grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 21 CFR 10.35 guidance and sample formats to prepare stay requests; ensure grounds justify an immediate stay if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect agency review and possible long timelines for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency staff evaluate petitions and FDA management ultimately decides whether to grant a petition. Evaluation may take several weeks to more than a year, depending on complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for potentially lengthy processing times and consider follow-up channels (e.g., contacting Dockets Management) for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in public meetings and hearings when available
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA schedules public meetings and hearings to discuss proposals; anyone interested may attend and, with advance notice, may comment on a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings often have virtual components and are often held in the Washington, D.C., area but sometimes elsewhere. Monitor the Federal Register for announcements and opportunities to present views.
